items.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020
items.q: I have a feeling it was probably Bobby Darin’s “Mack the Knife” with the big band

ctx.x: Ah — to live vicariously what others were doing. Do you recall what music you heard as a child that might have had something to do with your path in life?

You know I sort of do and sort of don’t. I remember my father gave me one of those clip- on unpowered radios. I don’t know if you remember that. It just has an alligator clip, you put it on your lampshade next to your bed and it receives stations. So I must have been like eight years old or something, and I remember hearing jazz and being knocked out, and I don’t even know what it was. I have a feeling it was probably Bobby Darin’s “Mack the Knife” with the big band, because that was something that would have…
Do you recall if you had a discussion with your parents about life as a musician or trying to fashion a career in music?
